Faction_StringTable.Cluster_A2M2_Desc: The planets in this region are known as "junkyards"- planets where scrap and components come and go daily. Scrap is sold by vultures, junkers, and even Mechwarriors who are looking to offload some junk- and gain a few extra cBills. The more inventive buyers are able salvage working components from the scrap, creating Frankenstein-like equipment that can turn a tidy profit.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_A2M1_Desc: This collection of star systems are known for their planets that house various refineries and industrial plants. Most of them are privately owned, and information on who exactly operates them- or what they produce- is scant. Rumor has it that many of the plants are in severe violation of the Ares Conventions, meaning that they are likely producing prohibited components related to chemical weapons.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_A2M3_Desc: While the wealthier residents of the Inner Sphere live in relative luxury, not everyone has access to the benefits of modern technology. In the almost countless agricultural worlds across the belt, the citizens who work the land live simple, if honest lives.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_AlarionPeriphery_Desc: Deep in Lyran space, the Alarion Periphery is a collection of worlds that were once members of the ancient Rimworld Republic. For all intents and purposes, they are independent nations, despite being in Lyran territory. This relative freedom from the Commonwealth means that this area is lawless, wild, and subject to violent conflict.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_BackwaterRegion_Desc: This rimward region of the Sian Commonality is remote enough from important manufacturing centers and the halls of power to be often viewed as only one step removed from the Periphery. Rumors of lostech and Star League–era technology abound. Many fortune seekers end up here, but few are those who find any real measure of success.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_MysteriousInvaders_Desc:
Mysterious Invaders from the void have declared war on the periphery!

These systems are sparsely populated and defended by small pockets of fighters that do not pose a significant military challenge.

As such, a huge payday awaits any outfit brave enough to head to the periphery and reinforce these toothless systems.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_CJF_InvasionCorridor_Desc: Worlds in The Lyran Commonwealth and Free Rasalhague Republic are under siege from two powerful Clan forces, including the Jade Falcons. Taking a contract in this area will not be the faint of heart, but there's a lot of bragging rights, and C-Bills up for grabs in signing up for this gig.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_CSJ_InvasionCorridor_Desc:
There are whispers that word has come down from Theodore Kurita himself that the Smoke Jaguars have their sights set on sinking their teeth in Combine Capital world of Luthien. 

The Smoke Jaguars reputation during this invasion is enough to scare anyone off from taking a job where they might show up. However, it also means that the merc outfit willing to put its neck on the line will secure a massive bag for taking this on. 

It's on you, mercenary Commanders, to weigh the risk vs reward on this one.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_CWF_InvasionCorridor_Desc:
One thing you can count on during this invasion - peace never lasts.  After a year without a shot fired, Clan Wolf has resumed their attacks on Commonwealth worlds of Temar, Sevren and Laurent.

There are lucrative pay days on the table for outfits willing to aid these worlds to stymie the powerful Wolves.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_CGB_InvasionCorridor_Desc:
Clan Ghost Bear is pushing hard across a wide stretch of Combine territory — not just one or two hotspots, but threatening to spread to their Capital world of Alshain. 

The DCMS is stretched thin, and the cracks are starting to show.

No official contracts, of course. The Combine would rather choke on their swords than admit they need help. But we’re hearing the same thing from multiple sources: planetary governors, regional generals, and even some yakuza-backed militias are looking to bring in outside guns. Quietly. Fast -  so there is a potential windfall for an outfit willing to sign up and stem the tide on these Combine worlds.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_ShippingRoute_Desc: This region encompasses one of the most heavily trafficked parts of the Federated Suns, owing to the trade routes employed by many high-profile corporations for transporting supplies and goods throughout the nation. Although this area does not see as much open warfare as systems immediately bordering the Draconis Combine, the mercantile trade throughout the region draws inordinate levels of pirate activity, and thus provides lucrative opportunities for mercenaries on both sides of the coin.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_KuritaDavionFrontline_Desc: The ongoing power struggle between House Kurita and Davion is not contained to one individual cluster, as their conflict spans far across their territorial border. While the Federated Suns pushes to reclaim former planets, the Draconis Combine is mounting its own separate push into enemy territory. Driven by its philosophy of total conquest of the Inner Sphere, the military arm of House Kurita is driving aggressively into Davion territory.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_DavionBorderlands_Desc: The worlds of the Draconis March region of the Federated Suns are in a constant state of flux due to the bloody war of attrition with between House Davion and its perennial enemy, House Kurita. The Draconis March represents the forefront of the conflict between these two nations, and planets change hands frequently.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_AddicksPDZ_Desc: The Draconis March region of the Federated Suns is already a harsh place to live. Constant fighting with the 'Dracs' for 3 centuries has left many of these worlds with deep scars.  The Addicks polymorphous defense zone is no different, and worse still being right at the heart of the Inner Sphere.  Sandwiched between worlds controlled by Kurita and Liao, and next door to Terra itself, this area is always on guard.  The conflict has also left many of these systems without the resources to build infrastructure, or fund education, making these once productive worlds feel like a backwater.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_MercenaryRow_Desc: The primary headquarters of Nik’s Cavaliers was located within a cluster of star systems known for housing various Mercenary outfits and freelancers. These companies shared an informal, if shaky alliance to stay out of each other’s systems. Now with the arrival of the Black Inferno, all bets are off, and the various companies are looking to capitalize amidst the chaos.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_BitterWorlds_Desc: Located near the furthest edges of the Inner Sphere, the Bitter Worlds are a collection of planets that have typically harsh, extreme climates. Only a handful of civilian settlements exist in the rare temperate biomes.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_TaurianCorridor_Desc: Members of the Taurian Concordat live under the constant threat of invasion from Federated Suns forces. To the Federated Suns however, the Taurians are nothing more than an inconsequential blip on their outer periphery, and often receive little attention. However, the neighbouring Capellan forces often instigate the two regions into battle, in order to spark conflict deep in Federated Suns territory.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_OutworldsAllianceBorder_Desc: A collection of periphery states, the Outworlds Alliance are pacifists by nature, and typically neutral. However, their position on the border of Davion and Kuritan territory means that the Outworlds Alliance is a hotbed for activity. The territory is a valuable tactical area, and the two great houses often use the region as a bed for proxy battles- much at the cost of its citizens.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_InfernosWake_Desc: The Black Inferno has left a trail of death and destruction in their campaign of violence. The nearby systems, home to sparsely populated agricultural and industrial worlds, have all suffered greatly. All that remains in this ravaged part of the Inner Sphere are desperate civilians and advantageous vultures looking to pick at the scraps.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_SilverFields_Desc: This region was formerly known mostly for the presence of its trading posts and shipping routes. However, after the discovery of veins of silver in some its the planets, the region has seen new life as a mining hotspot. This has come at a cost however, as the companies that were meant to service the local populace have up and left, choosing to pursue raw resources rather than feeding civilians.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_JuneCombatTheater_Desc: A Davion administrative military district, this region holds significant military presence due to its long history of fighting amongst Capellan and periphery forces. Despite the relative level of peace compared to its heyday in the Davion Civil War, this region is still well known for frequent, often violent military battles with invading forces from the edge of the Inner Sphere.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_ApexMiningSyndicate_Desc: The ore- and gas-rich systems in this region are a hotspot for extraction, mining, and industrial activity. The Apex Mining Syndicate, more commonly known as the AMS, all but outright own the planets within this area. The AMS operates and runs not only the extraction facilities but also the towns and cities in which the company’s employees live, resulting in more of a serfdom than a democracy. There are rumblings that the downtrodden workers are growing tired of the AMS’s rule.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_FledglingPeripheryRealm_Desc: The citizens of this region, far from the happenings of the Davion capital, have long felt disassociated with the Federated Suns identity. Tensions have reached a breaking point after years of residents having to defend their land from raiders, all while being ignored by the Federated Suns government.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_EdgewardOperationalArea_Desc: This cluster of systems acts as the regional command area for the Federated Suns Armed Forces. With very little civilian governance, the majority of residential and industrial areas are primarily operated and owned by the Federated Suns Military Command. Despite their high presence, daring bandits and marauders were still known to execute the occasional raid in this space.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_DavionKuritaFrontline_Desc: The Davion-Kurita conflict is one of the most bitter and storied rivalries in the Inner Sphere. The acrimonious events of the First Succession War planted a deep-seated hatred on both sides of the border—a grudge that still burns deep within First Prince Hanse Davion. Hanse is leading an aggressive series of attacks into Kurita space, aiming to reclaim Davion planets that have been lost more than 200 years ago. The perpetual war between the two Great Houses provides plenty of opportunities for mercenaries willing to get their hands dirty.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_DraconisBadlands_Desc: This group of systems is more sparsely populated due to years of economic depression from the depletion of local resources and lack of direct military importance. The region has, however, become a refuge for all sorts of criminals, bandits, and pirates trying to lie low. Efforts to curtail these predations often fall to mercenaries rather than Kurita troops.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_DroughtWorlds_Desc: The worlds in this region of the Draconis Combine have had their food, water, and other imported supplies severely rationed by their local rulers due to general state of malcontent and disorder caused by Unproductives. This strictly enforced state of conservation and privation has dragged on long enough that the planets here are derisively called the Drought Worlds.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_DuchyofAndurien_Desc: The Duchy of Andurien is an independent province of House Marik's Free Worlds League. Historically, the Andurien worlds have been disputed between the League and House Liao's Capellan Confederation. The Andurien people, however wish for independence from both nations, and on numerous occasions have called for secession from the Free Worlds League.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_DuchyofTamarind_Desc: The Duchy of Tamarind and its neighboring systems suffered brutally during the Succession Wars, and by the end of the Third Succession War, much of the duchy's industrial strength had been destroyed, its people impoverished. However, in 3013, valuable radioactive minerals were found in the Kosciusko system, which has led to a growing resurgence of prosperity for the population and a dramatic increase in the province's political and military significance.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_DuchyofTsitsang_Desc: The Duchy of Tsitsang is a collection of five systems in the Sarna Commonality of Capellan Confederation. This province is currently ruled by the self-centered Duchess Karis So. She cares little for the common people living under her rule, and only concerns herself with matters of the House of Scions, one of the Capellan Confederation's legislative bodies.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_FreeWorldsCommerceHub_Desc: This region near the heart of the Free Worlds League is a major commercial hub for business and commerce. Across the Inner Sphere, the League is known—and sometimes criticized—for its entrepreneurial spirit and business acumen. Despite the League's wide cultural diversity and generally democratic society, an undercurrent of discontent has long rumbled between the haves and the have-nots. Most of the worlds in this region belong to the Principality of Regulus, one of the League's founding provinces, and the Principality of Gibson; the rest are independent League planets.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_FreeWorldsInterior_Desc: These systems are mostly home to civilians and large residential settlements, and although this area's distance from the the nation's volatile borders lends to relative stability and safety, the Magistracy of Canopus lies only a few jumps away. Most of these worlds are independent and do not belong to one of the Free Worlds League's provinces, and each planet represents a diverse melting pot of cultures, people, and ideas.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_FreeWorldsLeagueShippingLane_Des: This region, sandwiched between the Duchy of Tamarind and the Abbey District, is an important hot spot for international shipping and trading, due to its prime location near the borders of the Lyran Commonwealth and the Circinus Federation. It is a place of extreme prosperity for those with an entrepreneurial spirit, but it also houses a considerably discontented lower class.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_WesterhandZone_Desc: Not all stars shine as brightly. Westerhand has long been overshadowed by the likes of Galatea and Solaris VII as both a mercenary's star and game world.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_GalateaZone_Desc: Thanks to a lucrative treaty, Galatea has long been one of the central hubs for mercenaries looking for work.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_EntertainmentWorld_Desc: The center for entertainment within the Magistracy of Canopus offering a wide range of options from theater to blood sport.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_Herotitus_Desc: The periphery's finest pleasure industry. If you want it, they have it.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_IndustrialHub_Desc: The worlds in this cluster are rich in not only scrap materials, but also cheap labour. As such, the planets within this system have become a hotbed for Mercenary companies looking to make repairs and 'Mech refits on the cheap.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_RogueCluster_Desc: Individual planets in the Draconis Combine are governed by a Chairman, who handles the day-to-day operations, such as setting the laws and controlling local militias. Even though the Coordinator must approve all policies and actions. In this region, a band of Chairmen have combined their forces and are enforcing their rule with an iron fist. Their strength in numbers seemingly bolsters them and protects them from repercussions from higher up the chain of command.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_AbandonedTerranWorlds_Desc: Located in close proximity to Terra, these worlds were some of the earliest to be settled by the first space-faring humans. The region was occupied in the early 21st century by the Terran Alliance, the first central government to control parts of the Inner Sphere. After the alliance devolved into tyranny, it was overthrown by rebellion, destroying almost every trace of the early rule. While the old settlers have been long gone, the spirit of violence and conflict still remains.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_TheGraveyard_Desc: This area has been nicknamed the Graveyard by superstitious locals. The worlds in this region are home to many ruins of old Star League–era facilities, and the evidence of ancient battles still remains. It is mostly home to agricultural and industrial concerns, but intrepid lostech hunters still frequent these systems.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_CommunicationsRelay_Desc: Little is known about the planets in this region, other than the fact that they are almost entirely under the possession of ComStar. Various records and documents seem to suggest that ComStar owns a number of communications relays on these mostly abandoned planets. Their purpose is unknown.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_OuterSettlements_Desc: Life is difficult in these settlements, far from the resources and infrastructure of central Inner Sphere. Life is a daily struggle to survive as the planets in this region are resource-starved, and heavily under developed. The only form of support is the occasional shipment of food and supplies from the Kuritan government.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_PeripheralWorlds_Desc: Save for a few lone settlements, the planets on these worlds are mostly abandoned, home to only Star-League era ruins. Despite the remote location, there have been persistent rumors that large military forces have been quietly operating in this region for quite some time.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_AncientStarLeagueGarrisons_Desc: The planets in this region were home to the remaining Star League Garrisons that operated in the twilight of the organization’s reign. Now, hundreds of years after the fall of the Star League, much of their old structures and establishments are long gone, eroded by constant war and scavenging.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_ProductionWorlds_Desc: This region is home to some of the oldest ‘Mech production companies, including Osaka Heavy Metrics, which has been in operation for almost half a century. Despite their longevity, even these companies have struggled, as the secrets of their once cutting-edge technology have become lost over time. With recent discoveries of once-forgotten memory cores, these manufacturing regions have seen a boom, which has led to great fortune, while putting a target on their backs.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_Lower-ClassKuritanWorlds_Desc: Many of the systems found in this region once belonged to the Principality of Rasalhague, which was conquered and absorbed by the Draconis Combine in 2330. The residents of these lower-class worlds generally suffer the most out of the Combine's populace, due to the nation's strict, militaristic society.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_PiratesEdge_Desc: The residential planets in this region are about as close to the edge of the Inner Sphere that most sane civilians will go. Located treacherously close to infamous pirate systems, these planets are under constant attack from the marauding bands. With its far distance to any Kuritan military hubs, the local prefecture’s government often resorts to hiring mercenary companies to keep its residents safe.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_RefugeeHideout_Desc: This region was flooded with Marik citizens who had been driven out from their homes by Black Inferno raiders. After the raids had passed, the Governor of this region refused to provide the refugees transport home, instead keeping them in detention. It is suspected that Liao's detention of the Marik refugees is to serve as a form of silent, economic warfare.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_SianCommonality_Desc: The Sian Commonality is the largest and most affluent region within the Capellan Confederation. In addition to the Confederation's capital of Sian, the commonality boasts the most developed worlds, the most valuable industry, and the most prestigious nobles in the entire nation.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_LiaoDavionBorder_Desc: The shared border between the Capellan Confederation and the Federated Suns is a regular hotbed of military activity. Border raids are incredibly common in both directions, but the tiger's share of offensive military action in this rivalry between the two nations is upheld by House Liao, due to House Davion focusing more of its attention on the volatile Draconis Combine border.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_LyranMilitaryStrongholds_Desc: This region of the Lyran Commonwealth is a hub for military facilities, strongholds, and command-base planets. While the Lyran Commonwealth Armed Forces are well equipped and boast the best BattleMechs money can buy, the organizational structure itself suffers from extreme bloat. Many individuals have risen through the ranks within the military not due to skill or merit, but because of networking, noble blood-ties, or political connections. This has created a top-heavy upper command that is all too often incompetent and slow to adapt to changes. While the LCAF is attempting to reduce these problems by phasing out these so-called "social generals," their incompetencies and poor decisions still haunt the Commonwealth and its military endeavors.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_StewartCommonwealth_Desc: The Stewart Commonwealth was a founding member state of the Free Worlds League, and its leaders in House Stewart remain strong and vocal supporters of House Marik. Like many of the Free Worlds League provinces, the Stewart Commonwealth is a stable democracy with a prosperous economy, rich culture, and generally high quality of life. The area is overall safe for the average citizen, but despite the diverse ethnic background of the League's populace, many people hold an open dislike for individuals with bionic enhancements, sometimes to the point of violence.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_MarikSteinerBorder_Desc: While all factions harbor deep-down resentment and rivalry with their interstellar neighbors, the relationship between Houses Marik and Steiner is more civil, if cautious. Both sides gain great economic and business benefits from their more peaceful relationship, and the two tend not to clash in the same way as many of the other Great Houses.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_OccupiedMarikTerritory_Desc: The planets in this system have been subject to decades of war and fighting, the scars of which can still be seen to this day. Under the weight of the substantial Free Worlds League military, the Liao government was forced to hand over a number of planets along their border. While owned by the Free Worlds League, Liao has never truly forgotten their loss, and still considers the region their birthright.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_BorderProtectorateRegion_Desc: In the days of the Star League, these worlds flourished under the control of the Terran Hegemony.  However, the Succession Wars resulted in many of these planets changing hands several times, often losing factories and manufacturing facilities each time.  Most of the factories are gone now, relocated to safer worlds away from this hotly contested border zone.  Despite their recent lack of economic standing, these systems are still heavily guarded, as no one is keen for them to change hands again any time soon.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_VacantWorlds_Desc: On the rimward fringe of House Marik space, this strange collection of systems gives even the most seasoned spacer captains cause to be wary. Numerous JumpShips and DropShips have traveled through this cluster only to vanish and never be seen again. Whether these disappearances are the result of lawless bandits living on the outskirts or something more inexplicable, this region of the Free Worlds League is a source of great superstition.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_MarikLiaoBorder_Desc: The Free Worlds League and Capellan Confederation are constant rivals, though the blows dealt to House Liao and the Chancellor's single-minded focus on the Federated Suns has dulled the bitterness of this contention. Despite the cooling of overt hostilities, intelligence-gathering border raids are still common all along this border. House Marik remains forever cautious of the Capellan Confederation and its federal and provincial military forces are always ready to counter Capellan adventurism.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_RasalhagueOuterReaches_Desc: Members of Rasalhague region can proudly trace their lineage back to the Scandinavian nations from Terra. In the centuries since settlement, the Draconis Combine have made numerous attempts to stamp out the Rasalhague culture, to mixed results. The ultimate goal of the Rasalhague people is to operate and survive as their own independent state, where they can freely practice their customs and way of life. The Lyran Commonwealth, sensing an opportunity to form a buffer state between the Draconis Combine and themselves, support the foundation of an independent Rasalhague Republic.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_RebelliousLyranProvince_Desc: Much of the Lyran Commonwealth's consistent success and stability is due to its democratic representation, which is rooted in the principles of ancient Athens. A far cry from the totalitarian rule of other Great Houses, the Commonwealth often utilizes a hands-off approach to its regions and provinces. As such, some provinces remember their ancient roots as independent realms, and constantly buck against the Archon's rule on Tharkad. The Isle of Skye is one such province. Some within the region are happy citizens of the realm, while others are looking to rise up and attempt a bid for independence. This issue has sharply divided this region, and tensions are beginning to boil over.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_SteinerKuritaLinchpin_Desc: Located precariously on the border of Steiner and Kuritan space, this region is equal parts a crucial frontline and important commercial and manufacturing region. Located in the middle of the territory is Port Moseby, a major spaceport and commerce hub that has flourished due to its location. Its prosperity however makes it a great target, and numerous proxy battles are fought by opposing sides all along this space.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_AlarionProvince_Desc: An area known for its abundant resources, often untapped given how sparsely these planets are populated.  Many of these worlds are simple places, laid-back and relatively independent, with the notable exception being Alarion itself.  While one of the more recent to be colonized, it's now a heavily industrialized world, home to numerous orbital factories and shipyards including the only WarShip production facility in the Lyran Commonwealth to survive the Succession Wars.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_CoreSystems_Desc: The worlds here are close enough to the capitol, Tharkad, that they've become not only a hub of commerce and news, but political rivalry.  Being so far removed from any real military conflict coupled with an abundance of trade means these worlds are full of those who will do anything to get ahead, and willing to pay well for someone to do it for them.  In fact, the region is well known for being quite friendly to mercenaries, having a long history of paying well, despite the reputation for bribery and corruption among the ruling class.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_OutworldSystems_Desc: Located far from the bustling city-worlds of the inner sphere, the planets in this region of space have been historically isolated and uneventful. Due to it's isolation, in 2756, regimental soldiers stationed in the region founded their own leisure sports leagues. Hundreds of years later, these leagues have flourished into lucrative, high-revenue organizations.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_LeisureIndustries_Desc: In an attempt to undercut the operations of numerous crime syndicates, the Steiner government provided sweeping legislation changes to establish this region as an area for relaxation and leisure. The region has become a significant tourist attraction, with the planet, Kooken’s Pleasure Pit being the crown jewel. However, despite the popularity, fighting within the fringes of the region still rages, especially amongst the criminal organizations.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_PirateWorlds_Desc: Tucked away on the far edges of the inner sphere lay the notorious Pirate Worlds. Home to countless bands of pirates, marauders, and bandits, it's unknown what secrets these oft unexplored systems contain.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_SteinerKuritaBorder_Desc: This region is home to fierce fighting between the Lyran Commonwealth and the Draconis Combine. While House Kurita expends more energy on its rivalry against House Davion, the Kuritans are still eager to destroy their House Steiner neighbors whenever the chance arises.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_Sarna_Desc: Once the seat of power for the Sarna Supremacy, one of the early intergalactic nations of the 22nd Century and one of the four nations that combined to form the Capellan Confederation, Sarna has maintained an allure of symbolic prestige and significance to the Confederation for generations.  But the meat grinder of the Succession Wars has made Sarna a shell of its former self. What was once a thriving system of nine billion souls has seen its population erode down to only two and a half billion after 300 years of perpetual warfare.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_AgriculturalBelt_Desc: There are few in the Inner Sphere that are lucky enough not to worry about constant warring of the great houses. In this Agricultural Belt of Davion space, the majority of the populace lived peaceful, if mundane lives. Now with increased bandit activity, the working-class residents of this area are now living in constant fear.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_NoMansLand_Desc: While technically under the rule of House Steiner, most people refer to this cluster of systems as No Man's Land. The title refers to the region's general lack of governmental and military oversight- and it's heavy presence of bandits, outlaws, and mercenary groups. This region is home to all manner of illicit and illegal activities.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_DraconisResidentialWorlds_Desc: The planets in this region are home to primarily residential planets, due to their proximity to crucial supply routes and manufacturing hubs. Despite being relatively flush with resources, life here is not easy, as Kuritan citizens have to worry about danger from all sides. Tensions with the nearby House Steiner mean that even the most sleepy settlement may turn into a front line battleground. Meanwhile, the region's nobleman rules with an iron fist, and his constant demands for tribute are beginning to economically harm his very own subjects.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_GameWorld_Desc: Home of the Solaris VII Games, the Inner Sphere's premier 'Mech combat spectacle in some of the largest, most well known arenas.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_Tigress_Desc: Due to a natural ecology mirroring that of Terra, Tigress was an early target for settlement as humanity began colonizing the stars. The rise of the Terran Hegemony saw great wealth and prosperity come to Tigress creating a beacon of higher education and wealth within the Terran Corridor that has continued long after the Hegemony's collapse.  During the 3rd Succession War, Tigress was gifted to the popular Laurel family by Tormax Liao. Since then, the local populace have fondly taken to referring to Tigress as "Laurel's World."
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_Tikonov_Desc: Colonized in the early 22nd century by Terran settlers, the resource rich Tikonov system quickly rose to become one of the most influential systems within its region of space spawning one of the early intergalactic nations of the 23rd century, the Tikonov Grand Union. Eventually absorbed into the growing Capellan Confederation, heavy investments into defending Tikonov's sprawling mining, heavy industry, and 'Mech manufacturing operations have turned the world into what many consider an impenetrable fortress.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_Rashpur-OwensManufacturingWorlds: The last major DropShip and JumpShip manufacturing facilities in the Capellan Confederation are located here. House Liao, continually beaten down by rivals in the Succession Wars, has seen its territory drastically shrink, and the Confederation's once mighty manufacturing industry has likewise deteriorated and withered.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_DLC7_HiddenSystems_Desc: There is on offer on the table to push beyond the edge of the map and head into an uncharted region of space, survey unknown systems, and report what you find — or deal with what finds you. There are no specifics. No maps. No confirmed hostiles. Just jump coordinates, and the possibility that you might find what you’ve been hunting for.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_Barcelona_Desc: A former Rim Worlds Republic fortress world originally built as a defensive bulwark to the Republic’s Apollo Providence. Eventually conquered by the Lyran Commonwealth during the Republic-Commonwealth War of the 2770’s, many of the republic’s defensive fortifications and network of ‘Mech trenches and defensive fortifications still stand today.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_ChaosMarch_Desc: The tattered remains of the Federated Commonwealth’s former Sarna March after the events of Operation GUERRERO. This former FedCom march has become a no-man's-land of dueling interests and contested territory between the fractured halves of the Federated Commonwealth, the Free Worlds League, and Capellan Confederation, both attempting to reclaim former territory originally lost during the Fourth Succession War, and various smaller powers looking to rid themselves of the Great Houses' influence entirely.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_LyonsThumb_Desc: Upon the formation of the Lyran Alliance, the self-crowned Archon, Katherine Steiner-Davion, quickly moved to declare the Lyons Thumb the sovereign territory of the Lyran Alliance. Despite the region including several Kuritan and Davion-administered systems. Looking to secure Combine worlds and de-escalate tension between the fracturing FedCom halves, Coordinator Theodore Kurita successfully petitioned ComStar and First Prince Victor Steiner-Davion to deploy nine regiments of DCMS peacekeepers to the region. A move seen by the Lyran Alliance as a naked attempt to annex the newly contested territory. Creating a territorial quagmire similar to the recently formed Chaos March.
Faction_StringTable.Cluster_Cambridge_Desc: One of the systems uncovered through the exploits of Jake Mason and Interstellar Expeditions, little was publicly known about Cambridge before an expeditionary force sent by AFFC hero Adam Steiner entered the system. Only to discover that the system housed a Defense Station that housed a small fleet of Jade Falcon Warships. A previous chance encounter in the system by ComStar’s Explorer Corps ended with the Falcons destroying the unwitting ComStar ships. All hands presumed dead.
